title: Quebec home built from 200,000 recycled bottles, assembled in just three days
summary_full: In a remarkable development, a two-bedroom house located in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, has been built using an innovative construction method known as PakVert. This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.
